subject: science
passage: The star-nosed mole, which lives in the wetlands of eastern North America, is nearly blind, yet it finds food with remarkable speed, whether digging through moist soil or hunting underwater. At the tip of its snout is a star-shaped ring of twenty-two fleshy rays covered with tens of thousands of tiny touch receptors. Tapping the ground around the animal roughly ten times per second, ______ allowing the mole to identify and swallow a small worm or insect larva in well under a second.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the mole's brain receives a detailed picture of every surface the star touches,
choices.B: the mole's brain is sent a detailed picture of every surface the star touches,
choices.C: a detailed picture of every surface the star touches is sent to the mole's brain,
choices.D: the star sends a detailed picture of every surface it touches to the mole's brain,

explanation.why: The introductory phrase "Tapping the ground around the animal roughly ten times per second" describes the star on the mole's snout. A modifier at the start of a sentence applies to the subject that comes right after the comma, so that subject must be "the star."
explanation.A: Incorrect. This makes "the mole's brain" the subject, so the sentence says the brain taps the ground.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This makes "the mole's brain" the subject again, so the brain is said to be tapping the ground.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This makes "a detailed picture" the subject, so the sentence says the picture taps the ground.
explanation.D: Correct. "The star" comes right after the introductory phrase, so it is clear that the star is what taps the ground.
